cards.explanation: The answer is that he rejoices in it. Paul says it plain: "Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you…" Rejoice, friends. When I stub a stamp on the counter, I do NOT rejoice. Paul is writing about suffering and the word he picks is joy.

The answer is body. Paul says he suffers "…for the sake of His body, which is the church." He even tells us what the body is, so nobody has to guess. I appreciate that, because a clearly labeled cookie box saves everybody a lot of guessing. The church is Christ's body.

The answer is False. Paul names who gave the commission: "I became its servant by the commission God gave me…" The commission came from God. Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles (Matthew 10:2), isn't mentioned in this passage at all. Paul says the commission was handed to him by God.

The answer is to fully proclaim the word of God. Paul says God gave him the commission "…to fully proclaim to you the word of God…" That's the whole job description. No fine print and no surprise extras. The commission is about getting the word out, and getting all of it out.

The answer is False. Paul says the mystery "…was hidden for ages and generations but is now revealed to His saints." The hiding is in the past, and the revealing is now. That's the good news in this verse.

The answer is True. Paul says God has chosen "…to make known among the Gentiles the glorious riches of this mystery…" The Gentiles are the non-Jewish nations. So the riches of this mystery aren't kept in one corner, and they're meant for them too.

The answer is Christ in you, the hope of glory. Paul puts it in one line: "…which is Christ in you, the hope of glory." The mystery isn't a rule or a riddle, it's Christ Himself. And he says it's for you, friends, which is the best part.

The answer is perfect. Paul says he teaches everyone with all wisdom "…so that we may present everyone perfect in Christ." Notice the last two words, in Christ. That's where the perfect part happens, so nobody has to bake it alone. I couldn't get a cookie perfect on my own in a hundred batches.

The answer is Laodicea. Paul says he's struggling "…for you and for those at Laodicea…" Laodicea is another place with believers. Later he tells the Colossians to make sure his letter is also read in the church of the Laodiceans (Colossians 4:16). His care reaches past one town.

The answer is love. Paul wants them "…encouraged in heart, knit together in love…" Knit is a great word. Think of a sweater: pull one thread and the whole thing feels it. What holds these believers together is love.
The answer is all of them. Paul says it: "…in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge." All. Not most, not a few. Paul leaves not one treasure out of Christ.

The answer is so no one deceives them with smooth talk. Paul gives the reason himself: "I say this so that no one will deceive you by smooth rhetoric." Smooth rhetoric is polished talk. Paul wants them to know Christ, so that no one deceives them that way.

The answer is False. Paul says, "For although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit…" He isn't there in person. He's writing a letter. He still wants them to know he's with them in spirit.

The answer is faith. Paul says, "…I delight to see your orderly condition and firm faith in Christ." He's absent in body, and he's still delighted by what he sees in them. A firm faith is a good thing to be known for, friends.
